title: Hybrid seatless license + support-credit packaging and SQ harmonization experiment for Private/VPC on-prem
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Run a controlled experiment that bundles a lightweight seatless base license for Private/VPC deployments with optional runtime add-ons (GPU pools, KV cache retention, premium quantization profiles) sold as time-bound support credits. Simultaneously create a consolidated Security Questionnaire (SQ) playbook and artifacts library to accelerate RFP responses. Goal: reduce procurement friction for mid-market/enterprise customers while preserving predictable revenue and limiting long-term upgrade overhead.

Background/context: Procurement cycles for Private and VPC customers often stall because sales and security teams must negotiate three separate axes: a core license fee (hosted on-prem runtime), ongoing support SLA, and periodic upgrade windows/managed upgrades. Engineering prefers minimal variance in packaging to reduce product surface area for upgrades. Customers prefer predictable pricing and a clear upgrade cadence.

Hypothesis: Packaging a predictable, lower-friction "seatless" base license (flat annual license keyed to deployment footprint) plus purchaseable, time-limited "ops credits" for higher SLAs and expedited upgrades will increase RFP-to-contract conversion rate by >20% and reduce average time-to-close by 15%. The SQ playbook will reduce security review iterations by 30%.

Success metrics: "ARR from Private deals won", "RFP cycle time (days)", "Number of SQ iterations per customer", "% of customers selecting premium ops credits", "Support cost delta vs. baseline".

Audience: Sales-led enterprise motion, Solutions Engineering, Legal, Security (GRC), Customer Success, Engineering (Private/VPC runtime).

decisions: Adopt seatless base license (annual, footprint-banded) instead of per-seat or per-instance pricing to simplify procurement and billing.

Offer ops credits in three denominations (Bronze: 40 credits/yr, Silver: 120 credits/yr, Gold: 400 credits/yr) where credits map to support actions (priority response, emergency patching, expedited upgrade scheduling).
Define upgrade cadence as quarterly maintenance windows with one emergency patch window per month for Gold ops credit holders.
Create a single SQ playbook and a templated annex to customer contract to accelerate legal/security reviews.
alternatives_considered: Per-GPU annual license with dynamic billing — rejected due to complexity for procurement and noisy billing reconciliation.
Flat percent-of-ARR pricing — rejected because it misaligns for customers running large on-prem inference footprints with tight unit economics.
Free indefinite support + charged upgrades — rejected due to high operational cost risk for early customers.
tradeoffs: Simplicity vs. revenue granularity: footprint banding reduces billing complexity but may leave revenue on the table for very large customers.
Ops credit predictability vs. sell-through: credits guarantee margin protection, but customers may view them as nickel-and-diming unless value is clearly demonstrated.
Upgrade cadence rigidity vs. reliability: fixed quarterly windows improve engineering planning but reduce flexibility for customers needing urgent feature releases.
pilot_plan: Target pilots: PilotCust-CloudPay (mid-market fintech), PilotCust-MediServe (regional healthcare), PilotCust-DataWorks (AI-native SaaS)
Incentive: one-time onboarding credit equivalent to Bronze ops credits for first-year to reduce friction
Measurement: track RFP-to-PO days, ops credit conversion rate, SQ iterations per customer
